- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 70.93 or 71.17), leading to overprediction of subsequent values.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: tends to forecast downward after recent high prices, but true outcomes often continue upward or show stronger momentum.
- Forecast lags: model often predicts lower values than true outcome for the first 5–7 days, then catches up or exceeds later.
- High volatility in history (e.g., 70.93 → 71.17) leads to model overreacting and forecasting higher than true outcome.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of upward trends, especially when history includes multiple consecutive high values.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating the true price’s upward momentum in trending periods.
- When history includes a low value followed by a spike, model often fails to capture the full magnitude of the spike in the forecast.
